walkthroughs.body_html:
Circles = female · Squares = male · Shaded = affected.

If two unaffected parents have an affected child, the allele must be recessive.

If every affected person has at least one affected parent, the allele is usually dominant.

Cystic fibrosis is recessive (ff). Two carrier parents (Ff × Ff) have a 1-in-4 chance per child.

Huntington's is dominant (Hh). One affected parent gives each child a 50% chance.

Screening can detect both — but raises tough choices.

The ABO gene has 3 alleles: Iᴬ, Iᴮ, Iᴼ.

Iᴬ and Iᴮ are codominant — both show together → blood group AB.

Iᴼ is recessive. So Iᴬ Iᴼ = group A, Iᴮ Iᴼ = group B, Iᴼ Iᴼ = group O.

mcqs.q: Two unaffected parents have a child with cystic fibrosis. What does this tell you?
options: The allele is dominant
The allele is recessive and both parents are carriers
The child has a new mutation only
The disorder is sex-linked

mcqs.q: A person has blood group AB. What does this show?
options: Iᴬ is dominant over Iᴮ
Iᴮ is dominant over Iᴬ
Iᴬ and Iᴮ are codominant
Iᴼ is dominant

mcqs.q: What does it mean for an allele to be 'dominant'?
options: Arteries and veins both carry the same mixed blood through the body.
It is expressed in the phenotype when at least one copy is present (in a heterozygote).
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
A dominant allele is the most common allele in a population.

mcqs.q: What does a gene code for?
options: Typically a polypeptide (protein) — through transcription to mRNA and translation by ribosomes.
Each gene codes for an organ or body part as a whole.
Arteries and veins both carry the same mixed blood through the body.
A gene codes for a specific physical feature like eye colour directly.
